name: Never overwrite secrets / API keys / credentials files
description: Files matching well-known secrets patterns (.env*, secrets/, credentials*, *_key.txt, *_token.txt, etc.) must never be written, overwritten, or edited in place — these files often have specific structure that's easy to corrupt. Both operations are gated (W2-D audit H-08: the trigger was write-only, so edit-in-place bypassed the rule its own text claimed to enforce). Reads are NOT gated — read-only access is the rule's own suggested remedy. Default response is hard-pause requiring explicit operator authorization.

response.message:
⛔ SECRETS FILE PROTECTION TRIPPED

Attempted write/overwrite to: {file_path}

This file matches the secrets-protection pattern. Overwriting it could
destroy operator credentials. Edit-in-place is also risky.

To proceed, confirm in chat with the exact phrase:
  "Yes, edit secrets file {filename}"

Or cancel and use a different approach (read-only access usually works).

why_lethal: Lost API keys mean lost service access, broken production deployments, potential billing surprises if keys end up in version control. Recovery requires regenerating keys at every provider — measured in hours of work.
